brief: Nvidia's market cap round-tripped from $1T to a peak $5.8T and has fallen back below $4T to an 18-month low, worsened after CEO Jensen Huang admitted an affair with a woman US officials suspect is a Chinese spy, prompting a board probe. Goldman's Molavi argues bubbles and lasting value are separate things: tulips, the internet and Britain's 1840s railway mania (500 companies, 8,000 miles of track, costing more than the country's national income) all proved real, but early capital lost money once valuations decoupled from cash flow, and the eventual value went to users, not builders. Today's AI trade is riskier because industries now feed AI circularly (Nvidia-OpenAI, Nvidia-Intel, Oracle-Nvidia, hyperscaler stakes in AI startups) and runs increasingly on debt, SPVs and vendor financing among a few companies, so losses may not stop at stock prices. Structurally, passive/index flows into an increasingly narrow market (60%+ of H1 gains from 6 stocks) built a momentum factor that unwound violently, giving back all its 2026 gains in weeks. Forward P/E near 18x is 'cheaper rather than cheap' against 2009/2020/2022 troughs, and could reverse if AI capex slows and 30%-plus earnings growth turns with it.
